correctness.rationale: For the exact twelve-vertex labelled edge list, complete host-graph BFS and exhaustive distance-signature enumeration independently reproduce no resolving set of size at most three and 146 resolving four-sets. Adjacency of bases in the jump graph is symmetric difference of cardinality two; for sliding, its two vertices must be a host edge. All-source BFS on the resulting graphs confirms connectivity, 928 and 452 edges, radii 4 and 4, diameters 4 and 6, slide eccentricities 4:2, 5:104, 6:40 and exactly centers {2,8,9,11} and {3,6,7,10}. All 10585 unordered distinct pairs give jump excesses (10367,218) and slide excesses (4463,4944,1070,92,16) relative to 4−|S∩T|. The proof covers only minimum vertex-resolving sets and single simultaneous replacements. Replay: python3 /workspace/review_checks/1.py; saved output /workspace/review_checks/1.out. This was a fresh finite computation, distinct from inspection of the frozen verifier evidence.

value.rationale: The Chvátal graph is a classical small regular high-chromatic host with independent interest. Its complete minimum-state mobility geometry quantifies a real difference between global and adjacency-constrained replacements that neither connectivity nor metric dimension records: only two optimal slide starting states and positive jump detours even without locality. The exact pairwise excess census supplies a directly usable small benchmark and a contrast with other hosts where every jump attains the exchange lower bound. This is not a claimed general algorithm or a family-wide result.
